trust_decision.summary: During XStream unmarshalling of attacker-submitted config.xml, the field/converter boundary decides which classes may be instantiated: nothing validates an element against the declared generic element type of a DescribableList/CopyOnWriteList field, and two non-configuration routing objects (PluginWrapper, InternalResourceRequest) are freely deserializable.

landing_point.why: The summary is attacker-controlled config.xml arbitrary type deserialization; this is the method that picks the converter for every persisted field and is the only place where the field's declared generic type is available.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /{item}/config.xml via AbstractItem.doConfigDotXml -> updateByXml -> Items.XSTREAM unmarshalNullingOut
POST /{item}/config.xml, reached through any DescribableList field such as View.properties
POST /{item}/config.xml (or CLI update-job): a smuggled hudson.Plugin with a wrapper field is then served through Plugin.doDynamic at /{item}/...
config.xml POST into any Stapler-reachable field, then a request to the resource-domain URL handled by InternalResourceRequest.doDynamic

O3_reason_to_dismiss: PluginWrapper is plugin-lifecycle metadata that is never part of project or view configuration, so a solver can call it unrelated to the config.xml list problem and fix only the element-type check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate elements that are subclasses of the declared element type must keep loading: plugin-provided ViewProperty/JobProperty subclasses and DescribableList subclasses such as View.PropertyList. A fix that rejects every element whose exact class differs, or blocks Describable deserialization wholesale, breaks plugin configuration and legacy documents.

O6_input_shapes: element whose class is a subtype of the declared element type (DescribableListSubtype, plugin-provided ViewProperty subclass) - must stay accepted
element with an explicit class= attribute naming a type outside the declared element type - must be dropped
null element - kept because only non-null items are checked
field with a resolvable generic element type, e.g. DescribableList<ViewProperty, ViewPropertyDescriptor>, from which the element type is extracted
raw or erased generic field type - element type is null and no check is applied

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Job.properties is a CopyOnWriteList<JobProperty>; its items are read by CopyOnWriteList.ConverterImpl, which never receives an element type, so any class can be stored in a job's config.xml properties list.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The code itself calls this a legacy shape ('this should have been DescribableList but now it's too late'), so a solver can dismiss it as an unrelated legacy field.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: two packages away (hudson.model vs hudson.util), reached from POST /{item}/config.xml

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PersistedList-typed fields (UpdateCenter.sites, PaneStatusProperties.collapsed, Fingerprint.facets) are read by PersistedList.ConverterImpl, which still builds a CopyOnWriteList.ConverterImpl with no element type; the published fix does not touch this file.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: PersistedList is internal plumbing for update-centre and fingerprint data, not user-edited project configuration.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing point, different file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ResourceDomainRootAction.Redirection, a second routing object in the same file with an attacker-settable url field and a doDynamic redirect, received no readResolve block, so it can still be smuggled in as a routable config object.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only yields an open redirect, so it looks out of scope against the impersonation and RCE described in the report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one nested class below the fixed site in the same file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A PersistedList.ConverterImpl(Mapper, Class) variant that carries the element type, mirroring the DescribableList change
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PersistedList.ConverterImpl already contains the identical CopyOnWriteList.ConverterImpl delegation that the published fix had to change in DescribableList, so a maintainer applying the same fix here is natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A persisted CopyOnWriteList<JobProperty> field that the new converter-selection branch could have covered
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix keys a new branch on the field type in RobustReflectionConverter; CopyOnWriteList is the obvious second case and already has converter support for elementType.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another private routing class next to InternalResourceRequest that would need the same readResolve block
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already holds a second routing class (Redirection) of the same shape, created from the same token-decoding getDynamic.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data (config.xml type confusion)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven, parent org.jenkins-ci:jenkins 2.1328.vfd10e2339a_19; modules core, test, war
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 with JenkinsRule; core/src/test/java/hudson/util/DescribableListTest.java and test/src/test/java/hudson/util/RobustReflectionConverterTest.java cover this area at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an element-type check only in DescribableList.ConverterImpl, or just reject the exact type used in the report's example, leaving CopyOnWriteList/PersistedList fields and the two routing objects untouched.
